description: Five fail-open advisory hooks: (1) UserPromptSubmit nudge deterministically steers Claude toward the nexus.memory_create / nexus.context_retrieve MCP tools on cross-session memory write/read intent (lifetime-axis rules shared with skills/nexus-memory/SKILL.md via hooks/rules.json); (2) SessionStart injection warm-starts a fresh session with the project's recent settled summaries (cross-container, provenance-annotated) via context/retrieve; (3) SessionEnd capture distills the session transcript into bounded activities and POSTs them to /activities/stream (P1 write side; backend worker extracts episodic memory keyed user_id=project); since plugin#49 a per-session watermark (persisted lines-consumed + sha256 prefix check in _hook_state session-capture state, newest 64 sessions) makes a resumed session POST only what the transcript gained — a lost/invalidated watermark costs one full resend which the backend's idempotent ingestion folds (nexus #468 A), adjacent identical payloads are folded client-side, and a non-zero deduped in the reply is logged on stderr as the watermark's self-check; (4) SessionEnd handoff-sync ingests the project's latest Aria session handoff (docs/handoff/) as a layer=session_summary episode, only when this container owns it (frontmatter owner-container uuid == this container's aria uuid) -- it does not filter candidates by owner while locating the newest one, only refuse the write afterward -- idempotent via the shared _ingest_client (workflow B, change 2 TASK-005); (5) SessionEnd memory-sync ingests this project's Claude Code auto-memory files (<CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or ~/.claude>/projects/<memory dir key>/memory/*.md, MEMORY.md excluded) as layer=fact rows, at most 5 files per run (dirty files first, then a persisted cursor over not-yet-synced files), external_id prefixed `<memory dir key>/<slug>` so two memory directories sharing a user_id/container_id never collide -- same idempotent _ingest_client, plus its own one-time-per-state orphan reconciliation (workflow C, change 2 TASK-006). All are advisory only — never block the prompt, session startup, or teardown; fail-open exit 0. TWO FIELDS BELOW ARE LOAD-BEARING, do not tidy them away: SessionEnd `timeout: 60` — the host gives all SessionEnd hooks (capture, handoff-sync and memory-sync alike) a SHARED ~1.5 s wall-clock budget, and a timeout declared HERE (plugin hooks.json) does NOT raise it (code.claude.com hooks doc: "Timeouts set on plugin-provided hooks don't raise the budget"; verified on Claude Code 2.1.312, #56: a same-session controlled run where these plugin hooks declared 60 s while an undeclared 3 s sibling hook was still cancelled). Raising the budget takes a settings-file per-hook `timeout` (capped at 60) or the `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSIONEND_HOOKS_TIMEOUT_MS` env var (since 2.1.268 it also sets the per-hook timeout of hooks without their own) — without one of those, memory-sync (~7-9 s, 9 network calls in memory-rich projects) is cancelled at ~1.5 s on every real session end and, by design below, leaves no ledger row (#56). The `timeout: 60` field stays: it bounds each hook individually once the budget allows it and keeps the tested headroom over the hooks' internal deadlines. Each hook's own HTTP timeout is 8 s; SessionStart `matcher: startup|resume` — compact and clear also fire SessionStart, and re-injecting there spends a retrieval on a session that already has the brief. SessionStart `timeout: 30` is a backstop, not the mechanism; the default would be 600. All three SessionEnd hooks keep a deadline of their own (20 s each) and cap the ledger write at 2 s, so that they record `timeout` and exit 0 by themselves: a hook the host has to kill leaves no ledger record (under the default ~1.5 s budget this is the CERTAIN outcome for any SessionEnd hook slower than the budget — the 20 s internal deadline never engages because the host kill arrives first; #56), and for SessionStart its stdout is discarded. A test keeps each `timeout` above deadline + ledger cap, read from the code. (urllib timeouts are per socket operation, not per request, which is why the hooks cannot rely on them.)
